new_quiz.q: What does locomotion mean for a character?
choices: The way the character is lit in a level
All the ways the character moves around, such as walking and jumping
The list of bones in the skeleton of the character
The speed at which animations are imported
new_quiz.explain: Locomotion covers the basic movement of a character. A locomotion set joins these animations so the character changes smoothly from one to the next.

new_quiz.q: What does the blend space BS_Locomotion blend, and based on what?
choices: Idle, walk and run animations, based on Speed
Jump and land animations, based on IsFalling
Upper body and lower body, based on the spine
Two cameras, based on Direction
new_quiz.explain: The blend space mixes idle, walk and run as Speed changes. If you have strafe animations, it can also use Direction.

new_quiz.q: When does the blend space also need a Direction axis?
choices: When the character can jump
When the character has an upper body layer
When the level has stairs
When you have strafe animations, which move the character sideways
new_quiz.explain: Speed alone cannot tell forward from sideways. With strafe animations, Direction picks the animation that fits the way the character moves.

new_quiz.q: Which four states does the state machine of ABP_Locomotion have?
choices: Idle, Walk, Run and Sprint
Start, Update, Finish and Reset
Locomotion, JumpStart, JumpLoop and JumpEnd
Ground, Air, Water and Ladder
new_quiz.explain: Locomotion plays BS_Locomotion, so idle, walk and run share one state. The three jump states cover the take-off, the time in the air and the landing.

new_quiz.q: Which values from the character do the transition rules read?
choices: IsFalling and Speed
Health and Score
Pitch and Yaw
Count and Spacing
new_quiz.explain: IsFalling tells the state machine that the character is in the air. Speed tells it how fast the character moves on the ground.

new_quiz.q: The character is running and leaves the ground. Which value makes the state machine leave the Locomotion state?
choices: Speed becomes 0
IsFalling becomes true
Direction becomes negative
The UpperBody layer is linked
new_quiz.explain: A character in the air is falling in the sense of the movement system. IsFalling becoming true is the signal to go to JumpStart.

new_quiz.q: What do you add to ABP_Locomotion so that another Animation Blueprint can supply the upper body?
choices: A second state machine with four more states
A Timeline with a float track
A Data Table with one row for each bone
An Animation Layer Interface with a layer named UpperBody
new_quiz.explain: The interface defines the layer. The layer node sits after the state machine in the AnimGraph and passes the pose to whatever Animation Blueprint is linked.

new_quiz.q: What does the Layered Blend per Bone node in ABP_Locomotion_Upper do?
choices: It blends the walk into the run by Speed
It removes the legs from the pose
It blends an upper body animation over the input pose
It plays the jump animations in order
new_quiz.explain: The node blends a second animation in only from a chosen bone upward. Starting from the spine, the legs keep the locomotion and the upper body shows the new animation.

new_quiz.q: How is the upper body Animation Blueprint activated in the game?
choices: With Link Anim Class Layers when a key is pressed
With Play Montage on BeginPlay
With Set Actor Transform on Tick
With Get Data Table Row in the AnimGraph
new_quiz.explain: Link Anim Class Layers connects ABP_Locomotion_Upper to the UpperBody layer of the running Animation Blueprint. The layer then uses the linked graph.

new_quiz.q: Your new state machine never plays on the character. What do you check first in BP_ThirdPersonCharacter?
choices: That the camera boom is long enough
That the Anim Class of the Mesh is set to ABP_Locomotion
That the capsule has collision
That the character has a Health variable
new_quiz.explain: The Mesh plays the Animation Blueprint named in Anim Class. Until you set it to ABP_Locomotion, the character keeps using the old one.

new_quiz.q: How is the master sequence LS_Scene_Master built?
choices: As one long shot with one camera and no cuts
As a list of screenshots in a folder
From at least 3 shots in a Shots track, each its own Level Sequence
From one Level Sequence for each actor
new_quiz.explain: The master sequence holds the Shots track. Each shot is a separate Level Sequence, so you can work on one shot without touching the others.

new_quiz.q: What is a Spawnable?
choices: An actor that the sequence creates when it plays
An actor that is placed in the level by hand and never moves
A camera that follows the player
A render setting in Movie Render Queue
new_quiz.explain: A Spawnable exists only while its sequence needs it. The level stays clean, and each shot brings its own actors.

new_quiz.q: Which actors must be Spawnables in this scene?
choices: Only the floor and the walls
Only the Post Process Volume
Only the sky and the fog
Characters, cameras and shot lights
new_quiz.explain: These actors belong to the shots and not to the level. As Spawnables, they appear with the shot and are gone when it ends.

new_quiz.q: Which cameras does the scene need at least?
choices: Three static cameras
One following camera and one static camera
Two cameras on cranes
One camera on the character
new_quiz.explain: A following camera uses Look at Tracking, a rail or a crane. A static camera does not move, and the scene needs at least one of each kind.

new_quiz.q: Where do you place your cuts?
choices: On an action
At random moments
Every five seconds
Only at the end of the scene
new_quiz.explain: A cut on an action is hidden by the movement, so the edit feels natural. Cuts at random moments pull the viewer out of the scene.

new_quiz.q: Why do you use a lighting channel for the hero in at least one shot?
choices: So the hero is rendered in a separate file
So the hero casts no shadows
So a light can affect the hero without changing the rest of the set
So the hero is hidden from the camera
new_quiz.explain: Lighting channels decide which lights affect which objects. A light on the channel of the hero shapes the hero and leaves the set as it is.

new_quiz.q: How do you keep the brightness of the picture from changing by itself between shots?
choices: Add more lights to each shot
Use a longer master sequence
Disable the Camera Cuts track
Lock the exposure with Manual metering
new_quiz.explain: With Manual metering the camera does not adapt to bright or dark views. Your lighting decides the brightness of every shot.

new_quiz.q: How do you grade one single shot differently from the base look of the project?
choices: Change the base Post Process Volume during the render
Add a grade for that shot with a different Priority than the base Post Process Volume
Paint the colors into the textures
Render that shot in another project
new_quiz.explain: The base volume holds the look of the whole project. A second grade with a different Priority can take over for one shot.

new_quiz.q: Which settings does the Movie Render Queue render of this scene use?
choices: A PNG sequence and EXR files, a Temporal Sample Count of at least 4, and TAA disabled
One MP4 file, a Temporal Sample Count of 1, and TAA enabled
A JPG sequence only, with no anti-aliasing at all
One screenshot per shot, taken from the viewport
new_quiz.explain: The temporal samples do the smoothing, so TAA is turned off. You save these settings as a preset named MRQ_Scene.

new_quiz.q: What does your half-page breakdown contain?
choices: The names of all assets in the Content Browser
The full text of the documentation pages you read
The shot list, what each camera does, what the grade does, and your render settings
The time each render took, frame by frame
new_quiz.explain: The breakdown explains your choices. A reviewer can read from it why each shot, camera move and grade is there.

new_quiz.q: What is a GDD?
choices: A debug window for AI characters
A short written description of a mechanic
A Data Table with difficulty rows
A graph that runs the enemy
new_quiz.explain: A game design document describes the goal of a mechanic, its rules, its numbers and how it should feel.

new_quiz.q: Why do designers hand over a tuned system together with a document?
choices: The engine needs the document to compile
The document replaces the playtest
The document is shown to the player
So other people can understand and check the work
new_quiz.explain: A graph shows how something works, but not what it is meant to do. The document gives the intent, so others can check the result against it.

new_quiz.q: From which systems must your mechanic use at least one?
choices: A Behavior Tree enemy, EQS spot picking, a State Tree object, or AI Perception
Niagara, Chaos, Water, or Landscape
Sequencer, Movie Render Queue, Control Rig, or Take Recorder
Lumen, Nanite, Virtual Shadow Maps, or Path Tracing
new_quiz.explain: The quest is about an AI mechanic, for example a guard that hears you, searches for you, and then gives up. Each of the four systems is a way to build AI behavior.

new_quiz.q: How do you build the enemy for the mechanic?
choices: From a Static Mesh with a Timeline
From a Widget Blueprint with a button
From a copy of BP_ThirdPersonCharacter with its own AIController Blueprint
From the Level Blueprint with a Delay node
new_quiz.explain: The copy gives you a working character with mesh and movement. The AIController Blueprint is what controls it in place of a player.

new_quiz.q: What does the struct S_MechanicTuning hold?
choices: The meshes and materials of the enemy
3 to 5 numbers that change the feel of the mechanic
The text of the design document
The names of the playtesters
new_quiz.explain: The struct defines the tuning values of the mechanic. Each row of the Data Table then gives these values for one variant.

new_quiz.q: Which rows does the Data Table DT_MechanicTuning have?
choices: One row for each enemy in the level
One row for each playtest
Five rows: Goal, Verb, Rules, Numbers and Feel
Exactly 3 rows: Easy, Normal and Hard
new_quiz.explain: Each row is one difficulty variant with its own values. Three real variants make you feel what the numbers do.

new_quiz.q: How do you know that the mechanic is really driven by the Data Table?
choices: When you switch the row name, the behavior changes without opening a graph
The Data Table is the largest asset in the folder
The graph has no nodes left
The enemy stops moving when the table is open
new_quiz.explain: The row is read at Begin Play with Get Data Table Row, and its values are passed on. If a new row name gives new behavior with no graph edit, the data is in control.

new_quiz.q: Where does the mechanic sit in the graybox test space?
choices: Behind the player start, out of sight
Outside the test space
Between the player and the goal
On top of the goal, with no way around
new_quiz.explain: The space has one goal, such as reaching a door. With the mechanic between the player and that goal, every run tests it.

new_quiz.q: What must the one-page design document cover?
choices: The full graph, node by node
The goal, the core verb, the 3 variants, their feel, and how you tested it
The history of the project and the tools you installed
Only the values of the Hard variant
new_quiz.explain: The page lets a reader understand the mechanic and compare it with what is built. A mentor checks that the document matches the result.

new_quiz.q: You work alone and have nobody to playtest. What does the quest ask you to do?
choices: Skip the playtest and write the note anyway
Play only the Easy variant once
Ask the mentor to play it for you
Play each variant 3 times and record your time and result
new_quiz.explain: Several recorded runs per variant give you real numbers to compare. You then write what surprised you and what you changed afterwards.

new_quiz.q: When is a tool finished?
choices: When it compiles without errors
When it has more than ten settings
When another person can use it without you in the room
When you have used it once yourself
new_quiz.explain: A tool that only its maker can use is not done. The test is that someone else gets the job done with the tool and its guide alone.

new_quiz.q: Which three things must a finished tool do?
choices: Solve a real problem, handle wrong input, and come with a short guide
Run on every platform, use C++, and have a logo
Replace the editor, hide its settings, and run on Tick
Work only for its maker, need no input, and have no text
new_quiz.explain: These three points make a tool usable by others. Without them it either solves nothing, breaks on the first mistake, or cannot be understood.

new_quiz.q: How do you find the task that your tool should do?
choices: You pick the most complex feature of the engine
You copy a tool from the documentation
You wait until a mentor gives you a task
You ask another person which slow and repeated task annoys them
new_quiz.explain: A real problem comes from a real user. If you have nobody to ask, you take a slow, repeated task from your own work.

new_quiz.q: Which three forms can you choose from for your tool?
choices: A Level Blueprint, a GameMode, or a HUD
An Editor Utility Widget, a Scriptable Tool, or a Python script
A Material Function, a Niagara system, or a Data Table
A Behavior Tree, a State Tree, or a Blackboard
new_quiz.explain: All three run in the editor and can automate editor work. You pick one and explain your choice in two lines.

new_quiz.q: What is an Editor Utility Widget?
choices: A widget that is shown to the player during the game
A material that is used on editor icons
A panel that runs in the editor and is built like a Widget Blueprint
A plugin that must be bought on Fab
new_quiz.explain: An Editor Utility Widget gives your tool a user interface inside the editor. You build it with the same designer you know from Widget Blueprints.

new_quiz.q: What must the tool do when its input is wrong?
choices: Show a clear message that says what is wrong
Stop without any message
Carry on and guess the missing values
Close the editor
new_quiz.explain: The tool checks its input first. A clear message lets the user fix the problem, while a silent failure leaves them guessing.

new_quiz.q: What does the one-page usage document say?
choices: How you learned to build tools
Which nodes the graph of the tool contains
What the next version of the tool will do
What the tool does, how to open it, its settings, and one known limit
new_quiz.explain: These four points are what a new user needs. The known limit saves them from trying something the tool cannot do.

new_quiz.q: What does your before and after example show?
choices: The tool with a light theme and a dark theme
The same task done by hand and done with the tool, with the time each one took
The first and the last version of the code
The Content Browser before and after you renamed the tool
new_quiz.explain: The two times prove what the tool saves. Without the comparison, nobody knows if the tool is worth using.

new_quiz.q: How do you test the tool if you work alone?
choices: You read the code one more time
You use the tool right away while you still remember everything
You wait a day and then use the tool by following only the document
You skip the test
new_quiz.explain: After a day you have forgotten small details, so you are closer to a new user. Following only the document shows where it is unclear.

new_quiz.q: What do you do with what you learn from the test?
choices: You write down what was confusing and fix one of those things
You delete the usage document
You tell the tester to try harder
You add as many new features as possible
new_quiz.explain: Confusion in the test points at a weak spot in the tool or the document. Fixing one of these things closes the loop from feedback to improvement.
